spec1.name: impulse-learning-in-rpc-api-only
spec1.requirement: Remove ImpulseLearning.persistMappingRecord() - no local storage for learning data. All learning data must go to rpc-api via POST /v1/learning/record-turn

spec2.name: instance-invariant-storage
spec2.requirement: ImpulseLearning.persistMappingRecord() should save with project_id scope and sync to backend for cross-instance learning. Storage key should be ['learning', projectId, 'impulse-mappings', recordId]

conflicts.description: Spec 1 (impulse-learning-in-rpc-api-only) requires DELETING persistMappingRecord() to move all learning to rpc-api. Spec 2 (instance-invariant-storage) requires MODIFYING persistMappingRecord() to add project_id scoping and backend sync.

impactAnalysis.whatHappensIfSpec1Wins: persistMappingRecord() deleted. Learning data goes to rpc-api only. Instance invariance achieved via centralized backend (SurrealDB). instance-invariant-storage spec partially satisfied (backend sync achieved, but via different mechanism).
impactAnalysis.whatHappensIfSpec2Wins: persistMappingRecord() remains but with project_id scoping. Learning data duplicated (local storage + backend sync). Violates impulse-learning-in-rpc-api-only architectural boundary.
impactAnalysis.actualConflict: Both specs want learning data in backend, but disagree on whether local storage should exist.

resolution.recommendation: SPEC 1 WINS - impulse-learning-in-rpc-api-only supersedes instance-invariant-storage for learning data
reasoning: Architectural boundary principle: Learning algorithms belong in rpc-api only
Eliminates data duplication (no local storage copy needed)
instance-invariant-storage goal (cross-instance access) is satisfied via rpc-api backend
Simpler architecture: single source of truth (rpc-api) instead of cache + backend
resolution.implementation: DELETE persistMappingRecord() as planned. Learning data flows to SurrealDB via POST /v1/learning/record-turn. This satisfies both specs' goal of backend storage, but via cleaner architecture.

updatesRequired.spec2: Update instance-invariant-storage spec to acknowledge that learning data uses rpc-api pattern (no local storage). Mark impulse-learning.ts as OUT OF SCOPE for instance-invariant-storage.
updatesRequired.validation: instance-invariant-storage validation should NOT check impulse-learning.ts for backend sync. That's handled by impulse-learning-in-rpc-api-only spec.

conflicts.description: Both specs modify the same hook. Spec 1 wants sendToRpcApi() (HTTP POST). Spec 2 wants MCP backend sync. These are compatible if sendToRpcApi() goes through MCP layer.

impactAnalysis.compatibilityCheck: COMPATIBLE - Both specs want backend sync. Difference is in mechanism (direct HTTP vs MCP).
impactAnalysis.preferredApproach: Use MCP layer for consistency with rest of opencode architecture (vessel flow: opencode → MCP → rpc-api)

resolution.recommendation: HYBRID - Use MCP tool for learning data submission
reasoning: instance-invariant-storage establishes vessel flow pattern: opencode → MCP → rpc-api
Consistency: Other operations (activity save, impulse store) use MCP tools
MCP provides abstraction layer (can swap backend without changing opencode)
Both specs satisfied: backend sync achieved, learning data goes to rpc-api
resolution.implementation: Instead of direct HTTP POST in sendToRpcApi(), call MCP tool metabob_learning_record_turn(). MCP tool forwards to rpc-api POST /v1/learning/record-turn. This maintains vessel flow architecture.

updatesRequired.spec1: Modify enforcement to use MCP tool instead of direct HTTP POST
updatesRequired.mcpTools: Add metabob_learning_record_turn tool to metabob-cli MCP
updatesRequired.validation: Validation should check for MCP tool usage, not direct HTTP call
